implementation_approach: Implement order cancellation by extending the Order model with cancellation-related fields (status enum, cancellationReason string, cancelledAt timestamp), adding a cancelOrder API wrapper function following existing patterns in orderApi.ts, implementing a new POST /orders/:id/cancel route in the mock API client with validation logic to enforce business rules (time window checks of 24 hours from creation, status verification to only allow pending orders), enhancing OrderHistoryPage component with conditional cancel button rendering based on order eligibility, adding a confirmation dialog using inline state management (no new UI library), and updating localStorage persistence in orderStorage.ts to handle cancelled state. The implementation strictly follows established architectural patterns: API wrapper abstraction layer, React hooks for component state (useState/useCallback), mock client validation logic, error handling via ApiError class, and simple list rendering. Business logic centralized in mock client enforces: only orders in 'pending' status can be cancelled, only within 24 hours of creation, user must be authenticated.
coupling_observations: The implementation introduces moderate coupling points that are well-contained: (1) Order model extension cascades through API layer - any new field in Order interface must be handled in getMyOrders response and createOrder response, but this is localized to orderApi.ts wrappers; (2) Mock client.ts becomes the single source of truth for cancellation validation logic - centralizes business rules (time window, status checks) but increases file complexity; (3) OrderHistoryPage tightly couples data fetching, state management, and cancellation UI within same component - creates moderate complexity but avoids prop-drilling; (4) Cancellation state must coordinate with existing reviewStatus field - different lifecycle concerns (review availability vs order status), no semantic conflict; (5) Error handling integrates with existing ApiError infrastructure via errorMessages.ts - no new coupling, reuses existing patterns; (6) Storage layer maintains backward compatibility through optional cancellation fields; (7) No external library dependencies or cross-system coupling - purely internal feature. Overall coupling is acceptable - layered architecture (entity → API → storage → UI) prevents tight coupling across layers.
duplication_observations: Duplication is minimal due to strong existing abstractions: (1) API wrapper pattern well-established in orderApi.ts - cancelOrder function mirrors createOrder and getMyOrders structure exactly (single responsibility, consistent naming, error handling); (2) Async state management pattern exists throughout OrderHistoryPage - loading/error handling via useState/try-catch already used for initial order fetch, cancellation will reuse identical pattern; (3) Button component with disabled state already supports cancellation button requirements - no new variant needed; (4) Confirmation before action is new pattern - inline state management (useState for showing/hiding dialog) rather than new Modal component; (5) Error translation via errorMessages.ts reused - cancellation errors map to existing or minimal new codes; (6) Order persistence pattern mirrors existing saveOrder/replaceOrderHistory functions - no structural duplication; (7) Validation rules kept centralized in mock client - no scattered duplicate checks. Only minor duplication: confirmation dialog logic (show/hide state) is inline and cannot be reused until second feature requires it. Acceptable cost.
responsibility_observations: Proper separation of concerns maintains clean architecture: (1) Order model (entities/order/model.ts) defines data structure only - adds OrderStatus type ('pending'|'cancelled'), optional cancellationReason string, optional cancelledAt timestamp without validation logic; (2) orderApi.ts provides API abstraction - new cancelOrder(orderId: ID, reason?: string): Promise<Order> wraps POST endpoint, no business logic; (3) Mock client (shared/api/client.ts) owns validation and state transitions - time window calculation, status checking, order update logic; (4) OrderHistoryPage owns UI orchestration - conditional rendering of cancel button, confirmation dialog state, API call initiation, error display; (5) orderStorage.ts handles localStorage persistence - saveOrder function automatically persists updated order state, no special handling needed; (6) errorMessages.ts translates codes - optional new codes for 'order_already_cancelled', 'cancellation_window_expired'; (7) Button component is pure presentation. This clear separation enables isolated testing and future refactoring without cascading changes.
changeability_observations: The implementation establishes extensible patterns for future order state management: (1) OrderStatus enum is foundation for future states - can grow to 'pending'|'confirmed'|'ready'|'completed'|'cancelled'|'refunded'|'returned' with minimal changes to model and validation logic; (2) Cancellation time window is parameterizable - currently 24 hours, future requirement to make store-specific (some stores 2 hours, others 48 hours) requires moving calculation to mock client config, no client changes; (3) Optional cancellationReason field enables audit trail - future requirement for mandatory reason or reason categories only affects API validation, not UI unless displayed; (4) Confirmation pattern is reusable - next feature requiring confirmation (delete, return, reschedule) can inline same dialog pattern or extract to shared Modal component; (5) Error codes extensible - new cancellation scenarios don't break existing error handling; (6) Storage layer backward compatible - optional fields don't affect existing order deserialization; (7) Mock client validation ready for backend migration - logic can move to actual API endpoint without client-side changes; (8) Component hierarchy avoids early abstraction - OrderHistoryPage stays monolithic until multiple features justify extraction into OrderCard sub-component. Architecture supports clean evolution as feature scope grows.
